claims.evidence: This describes the generation of TWIST1 KO lines, shown in Figure 5A-B.

claims.claim: Myogenic cells at day 30 derived from TWIST1 KO clones did not express TWIST1 protein based on western blot experiment and antibody staining.
claims.source: Myogenic cells at day 30 derived from these KO clones did not express TWIST1 protein based on western blot experiment and antibody staining (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A) (TWIST1 was not detected in any of 1810 KO cells from three different clones), while TWIST1-positive cells were found in wild type (WT) (23.68 ± 2.25%, mean ± SEM).
claims.evidence: This describes validation of TWIST1 KO shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A.

claims.claim: TWIST1-positive cells were found in wild type (WT) at 23.68 ± 2.25%.
claims.source: Myogenic cells at day 30 derived from these KO clones did not express TWIST1 protein based on western blot experiment and antibody staining (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A) (TWIST1 was not detected in any of 1810 KO cells from three different clones), while TWIST1-positive cells were found in wild type (WT) (23.68 ± 2.25%, mean ± SEM).
claims.evidence: This describes quantification of TWIST1 expression in WT cells.

claims.claim: The levels of PAX7 expression in TWIST1 KO cells were comparable to that of the WT clones between day 25 and day 30 (9.29 ± 0.68% vs. 9.40 ± 1.35).
claims.source: First, the TWIST1 KO clones in the PAX7::EGFP reporter line were subjected to our myogenic specification protocol (Figure 5C). The levels of PAX7 expression in TWIST1 KO cells were comparable to that of the WT clones between day 25 and day 30 (9.29 ± 0.68% vs. 9.40 ± 1.35, Figure 5D and Figure 5—figure supplement 1B–C), demonstrating that TWIST1 KO does not affect the formation of PAX7+ skeletal muscle stem/progenitor cells during in vitro human skeletal muscle generation.
claims.evidence: This describes FACS analysis results shown in Figure 5D and Figure 5—figure supplement 1B–C.

claims.claim: TWIST1 KO does not affect the formation of PAX7+ skeletal muscle stem/progenitor cells during in vitro human skeletal muscle generation.
claims.source: First, the TWIST1 KO clones in the PAX7::EGFP reporter line were subjected to our myogenic specification protocol (Figure 5C). The levels of PAX7 expression in TWIST1 KO cells were comparable to that of the WT clones between day 25 and day 30 (9.29 ± 0.68% vs. 9.40 ± 1.35, Figure 5D and Figure 5—figure supplement 1B–C), demonstrating that TWIST1 KO does not affect the formation of PAX7+ skeletal muscle stem/progenitor cells during in vitro human skeletal muscle generation.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the TWIST1 KO experiments.

claims.claim: 69.88 ± 3.49% of Ki67+ cells were found in TWIST1 KO PAX7::EGFP+ cells, which was comparable to that of WT clones, indicating that TWIST1 did not affect cell proliferation capacity.
claims.source: Next, to see if TWIST1 has a role in cell proliferation of PAX7::EGFP+ cells, we tested their proliferation abilities during in vitro expansion. We found 69.88 ± 3.49% of Ki67+ cells in TWIST1 KO PAX7::EGFP+ cells, which was comparable to that of WT clones, indicating that TWIST1 did not affect cell proliferation capacity (Figure 5—figure supplement 1D).
claims.evidence: This describes Ki67 staining results shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1D.

claims.claim: The level of apoptosis (examined using Annexin V analysis) in TWIST1 KO PAX7::EGFP+ cells was similar to that of WT clones.
claims.source: The level of apoptosis (examined using Annexin V analysis) in TWIST1 KO PAX7::EGFP+ cells was similar to that of WT clones (Figure 5—figure supplement 1E).
claims.evidence: This describes Annexin V analysis results shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1E.

claims.claim: There was no difference in the fusion index (MF20 antibody staining) between TWIST1 KO and WT PAX7::EGFP+ cells, indicating that TWIST1 deletion does not cause any detectable defects in multinucleated myotube formation.
claims.source: To determine the functionality of TWIST1 KO PAX7::EGFP+ cells, isolated PAX7::EGFP+ cells were cultured until passage four and differentiated to myotubes in each passage (Figure 5F and Figure 5—figure supplement 1F). We found that there was no difference in the fusion index (MF20 antibody staining) between TWIST1 KO and WT PAX7::EGFP+ cells, indicating that TWIST1 deletion does not cause any detectable defects in multinucleated myotube formation.
claims.evidence: This describes fusion index analysis shown in Figure 5F and Figure 5—figure supplement 1F.

claims.claim: There are aberrant transcriptional patterns of PAX3, PAX7, MYF5, and MYOD1 during the myogenic specification in TWIST1 KO cells.
claims.source: Interestingly, there are aberrant transcriptional patterns of PAX3, PAX7, MYF5, and MYOD1 during the myogenic specification (Figure 5—figure supplement 2A), although the levels of PAX7::EGFP+ cells in WT and TWIST1 KO clones (at Day 25 to Day 30 of myogenic specification) are comparable (Figure 5D and Figure 5—figure supplement 2B–C).
claims.evidence: This describes qRT-PCR results shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2A.

claims.claim: The percentages of PAX7::EGFP+ cells in late passages (at passages 2 to 4) were significantly lower in TWIST1 KO PAX7::EGFP+ cells (15.98 ± 1.70% at passage 4) compared to the percentage of PAX7::EGFP+ cells in WT (29.80 ± 1.04% at passage 4).
claims.source: To test the role of TWIST1 in maintenance of PAX7 expression in the isolated PAX7::EGFP+ cells, we performed weekly FACS analysis during cell expansion for a month. While both WT and KO PAX7::EGFP+ cells showed comparable levels of PAX7 expression at the early passages, the percentages of PAX7::EGFP+ cells in late passages (at passages 2 to 4) were significantly lower in TWIST1 KO PAX7::EGFP+ cells (15.98 ± 1.70% at passage 4) compared to the percentage of PAX7::EGFP+ cells in WT (29.80 ± 1.04% at passage 4) (p values, 0.0983, 0.0008,<0.0001, and 0.0012 at passages 1, 2, 3, and 4, respectively) (Figure 5E and Figure 5—figure supplement 2B).
claims.evidence: This describes FACS analysis results during cell expansion shown in Figure 5E and Figure 5—figure supplement 2B.

claims.claim: TWIST1 deletion has a significant effect on maintaining PAX7::EGFP expression in putative human skeletal muscle stem/progenitor cells, but loss of TWIST1 has no effect on proliferation or apoptosis during in vitro expansion.
claims.source: These results revealed that TWIST1 deletion has a significant effect on maintaining PAX7::EGFP expression in putative human skeletal muscle stem/progenitor cells, but loss of TWIST1 has no effect on proliferation or apoptosis during in vitro expansion.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the TWIST1 KO experiments.

claims.claim: TWIST1 might have an important role in the maintenance of PAX7 expression in putative human skeletal muscle stem/progenitor cells.
claims.source: Taken together, our results demonstrated that TWIST1 might have an important role in the maintenance of PAX7 expression in putative human skeletal muscle stem/progenitor cells.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the TWIST1 KO experiments.

claims.claim: RNA-seq analysis was carried out for the purified cells from TWIST1 Knock-Out (KO) PAX7::EGFP+ cells.
claims.source: In order to understand the underlying mechanism of TWIST1's role in in vitro human myogenesis at the genome-wide level, we carried out RNA-seq analysis for the purified cells from TWIST1 Knock-Out (KO) PAX7::EGFP+ cells.
claims.evidence: This describes the RNA-seq experimental design for TWIST1 KO cells.

claims.claim: PCA showed that TWIST1 KO PAX7::EGFP+ cells were distinct from the other five cell populations in terms of genetic distance and relatedness.
claims.source: PCA showed that TWIST1 KO PAX7::EGFP+ cells were distinct from the other five cell populations in terms of genetic distance and relatedness (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A and Supplementary file 4, related to Figure 2C).
claims.evidence: This describes PCA results shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A.

claims.claim: The heatmap showed 643 differentially expressed genes between WT PAX7::EGFP+ cells and TWIST1 KO PAX7::EGFP+ cells.
claims.source: To identify differential gene expression between TWIST1 KO PAX7::EGFP+ cells and WT PAX7::EGFP+ cells, we performed unsupervised hierarchical clustering analysis (Figure 6A and Supplementary file 4). The heatmap showed 643 differentially expressed genes between WT PAX7::EGFP+ cells and TWIST1 KO PAX7::EGFP+ cells.
claims.evidence: This describes clustering analysis results shown in Figure 6A.

claims.claim: Out of 4317 genes highly upregulated over OCT4::EGFP+ cell populations, WT PAX7::EGFP+ cells and TWIST1 KO PAX7::EGFP+ cells had 1996 shared genes with GO terms of Extracellular Matrix Organization (GO:0030198), Muscle Filament Sliding (GO:0030049), and Collagen Catabolic Process (GO:0030574).
claims.source: To investigate the similarities and dissimilarities in the global gene expression between WT PAX7::EGFP+ cells and TWIST1 KO PAX7::EGFP+ cells, a Venn diagram was plotted (Figure 6B and Supplementary file 4). Out of 4317 genes highly upregulated over OCT4::EGFP+ cell populations, WT PAX7::EGFP+ cells and TWIST1 KO PAX7::EGFP+ cells had 1996 shared genes with GO terms of Extracellular Matrix Organization (GO:0030198), Muscle Filament Sliding (GO:0030049), and Collagen Catabolic Process (GO:0030574).
claims.evidence: This describes Venn diagram analysis results shown in Figure 6B.

claims.claim: The 1736 genes upregulated in TWIST1 KO PAX7::EGFP+ cells were classified to GO terms such as Translational Initiation (GO:0006413), SRP-dependent cotranslational protein targeting to membrane (GO:0006614), and Viral Transcription (GO:0019083).
claims.source: The 1736 genes upregulated in TWIST1 KO PAX7::EGFP+ cells were classified to GO terms such as Translational Initiation (GO:0006413), SRP-dependent cotranslational protein targeting to membrane (GO:0006614), and Viral Transcription (GO:0019083).
claims.evidence: This describes GO analysis results for TWIST1 KO specific genes.

claims.claim: The upregulated TFs in WT PAX7::EGFP+ cells included HES6, EGR2, YBX3, and TWIST1.

The upregulated TFs in WT PAX7::EGFP+ cells included HES6, EGR2, YBX3, and TWIST1.

claims.evidence: This describes differential TF expression analysis.

claims.claim: The GO terms indicated Response to Endoplasmic Reticulum Stress (GO:0034976, p value, 5.95E-04), Skeletal Muscle Tissue Development (GO:0007519, 9.35E-03), Skeletal Muscle Organ Development (GO:0060538, 1.06E-02), Muscle Organ Development (GO:0007517, 1.40E-02), and Transmembrane Transport (GO:0055085, 1.76E-02) in WT PAX7::EGFP+ cells.

claims.evidence: This describes GO analysis results shown in Figure 6D.

claims.claim: GO terms of Regulation of mRNA Processing (GO:0050684, 7.41E-05), Cell Division (GO:0051301, 1.96E-04), RNA Processing (GO:0006396, 1.83E-03), ER to Golgi Vesicle-mediated Transport (GO:0006888, 6.34E-03), and Wnt Signaling Pathway (GO:0016055, 7.63E-03) were enriched in TWIST1 KO PAX7::EGFP+ cells.

claims.claim: It has been demonstrated that Twist1 is directly bound to Pax7 locus in non-skeletal muscle tissues based on Chip-seq analysis by other groups.

claims.evidence: This references prior work on Twist1 binding, with citations.

claims.claim: The Wnt signaling pathway plays an important role in maintaining stemness of adult satellite cells.
claims.source: We focused on the WNT signal pathway among the prominent GO terms, because the Wnt signaling pathway plays an important role in maintaining stemness of adult satellite cells (Girardi and Le Grand, 2018; Jones et al., 2015; Biressi et al., 2014; Bentzinger et al., 2014; Bentzinger et al., 2013).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge about Wnt signaling, with citations.

claims.evidence: This describes experimental results with WNT activator shown in Figure 6F and Figure 6—figure supplement 1B.

claims.claim: Treatment of TWIST1 KO PAX7::EGFP cells with the WNT inhibitor (XAV939) chemical compound reversed the TWIST1 KO phenotype, but no statistically significant effects on maintenance of PAX7::EGFP expression were found.

claims.evidence: This describes experimental results with WNT inhibitor shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1C–D.

claims.claim: TWIST1 is crucial for in vitro expansion of PAX7::EGFP+ cells, and it is associated with the WNT signaling pathway.
claims.source: These data demonstrated that TWIST1 is crucial for in vitro expansion of PAX7::EGFP+ cells, and it is associated with the WNT signaling pathway.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the WNT signaling experiments.

claims.claim: The study presents a comprehensive analysis for the transcriptome of hPSC-derived myogenic specification.
claims.source: Here, we present a comprehensive analysis for the transcriptome of hPSC-derived myogenic specification.
claims.evidence: This is a summary statement about the study.

claims.claim: By utilizing multiple reporting hPSC lines, transcriptionally defined stages of human in vitro myogenesis were reconstructed and sets of novel genes including transcription factors were uncovered, followed by validation of a new gene, TWIST1.
claims.source: By utilizing multiple reporting hPSC lines, we reconstructed transcriptionally defined stages of human in vitro myogenesis and uncovered sets of novel genes including transcription factors, followed by validation of a new gene, TWIST1.
claims.evidence: This is a summary statement about the study's approach and findings.

claims.claim: The data provide insights into the dynamics of the transcriptome during in vitro myogenesis and demonstrate the ability to study significant mechanisms in a stage specific manner during embryonic myogenesis.
claims.source: Our data provide insights into the dynamics of the transcriptome during in vitro myogenesis and demonstrate the ability to study significant mechanisms in a stage specific manner during embryonic myogenesis.
claims.evidence: This is a summary statement about the significance of the study.

claims.claim: Genetic reporter stem cell lines are important tools to study transcriptional regulation and functions in various cell fate determination processes.
claims.source: As shown in stem cell research to isolate specific sub-populations during differentiation processes (Ganat et al., 2012; Tchieu et al., 2017), genetic reporter stem cell lines are important tools to study transcriptional regulation and functions in various cell fate determination processes, and they are useful to understand the dynamic fluctuations of expression of key transcription factors.
claims.evidence: This is a general statement about the utility of reporter lines, with citations.

claims.claim: Six individual 'knock-in' genetic reporter hPSC lines targeting key myogenic specification genes were successfully utilized in this study.
claims.source: In this study, we successfully utilized six individual 'knock-in' genetic reporter hPSC lines targeting key myogenic specification genes.
claims.evidence: This describes the experimental approach of the study.

claims.claim: The new reporter cell lines allowed prospective identification and purification of specific cellular populations with high purity during in vitro human myogenesis, leading to delineation of a comprehensive transcriptional landscape of human skeletal muscle development.
claims.source: These new reporter cell lines allowed us to prospectively identify and purify specific cellular populations with high purity during in vitro human myogenesis, leading us to delineate a comprehensive transcriptional landscape of human skeletal muscle development.
claims.evidence: This is a summary of the study's achievements.

claims.claim: The transcriptional similarity and disparity between PAX7 expressing cells (muscle stem/progenitor cells) and MYOG expressing cells (myoblast cells) has not been well characterized.
claims.source: Early embryonic myogenesis has been investigated in animal models, and key transcription factors, such as PAX7 and MYOG, have been discovered (Bentzinger et al., 2012; Kassar-Duchossoy et al., 2005; Parker et al., 2003); however, the transcriptional similarity and disparity between PAX7 expressing cells (muscle stem/progenitor cells) and MYOG expressing cells (myoblast cells) has not been well characterized.
claims.evidence: This is an assessment of the current state of knowledge, with citations.

claims.claim: By using PAX7::EGFP and MYOG::EGFP genetic reporter hPSC lines, two distinct but converged cellular populations during human in vitro myogenesis were captured.
claims.source: By using PAX7::EGFP and MYOG::EGFP genetic reporter hPSC lines, we were able to capture two distinct but converged cellular populations during human in vitro myogenesis.
claims.evidence: This describes a key finding of the study.

claims.claim: The list of enriched transcription factors in PAX7::EGFP+ cells, but not in MYOG::EGFP+ cells, include genes of the JUN signaling pathway family, such as JUN, JUNB and FOS genes, which are known to prevent the activation of MYOG.
claims.source: For instance, the list of enriched transcription factors in PAX7::EGFP+ cells, but not in MYOG::EGFP+ cells, include genes of the JUN signaling pathway family, such as JUN, JUNB and FOS genes, which are known to prevent the activation of MYOG (Li et al., 1992).
claims.evidence: This describes differential gene expression findings, with citation.

claims.claim: ID3, a well-known downstream target gene of PAX7 as reported in mouse skeletal muscle stem cells, is also expressed in the PAX7::EGFP+ cells.
claims.source: ID3, a well-known downstream target gene of PAX7 as reported in mouse skeletal muscle stem cells (Kumar et al., 2009; van Velthoven et al., 2017), is also expressed in the PAX7::EGFP+ cells.
claims.evidence: This describes gene expression findings, with citations.

claims.claim: The HMG family of DNA binding coding genes, including HMGB1, HMGB2, HMGA1, and HMGB3, are enriched in the PAX7::EGFP+ population, suggesting their potential roles in skeletal muscle stem/progenitor properties.
claims.source: The HMG family of DNA binding coding genes, including HMGB1, HMGB2, HMGA1, and HMGB3, are also enriched in the PAX7::EGFP+ population, suggesting their potential roles in skeletal muscle stem/progenitor properties.
claims.evidence: This describes gene expression findings and speculation about function.

claims.claim: The HMGB1 gene is heavily involved in regulation of proliferation and differentiation in other stem cell populations.
claims.source: The HMGB1 gene is heavily involved in regulation of proliferation and differentiation in other stem cell populations (Meng et al., 2018; Wang et al., 2014).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge about HMGB1, with citations.

claims.claim: Increased FOXO1 and FOXO4 transcription levels in MYOG::EGFP+ cells might be related to the proliferation ability of MYOG::EGFP+ cells, since the FOXO family contributes to proliferation of myoblasts through the AKT signaling pathway.

claims.evidence: This is speculation about gene function based on prior knowledge, with citations.

claims.claim: A list of genes coding for the ERK signaling pathway proteins, such as ATF4, TEAD4, and SNAI1, are enriched in the MYOG::EGFP+ population, suggesting that properties of myoblasts are related to the ERK signaling pathway as previously shown in animal studies.

claims.evidence: This is speculation about pathway involvement based on gene expression and prior knowledge, with citations.

claims.claim: The clustering analysis of gene expression data is beneficial for identification of novel genes, finding specialized functions associated with continuous biological events, and discovering transcriptionally distinct properties of defined stage-specific cell populations.
claims.source: The clustering analysis of gene expression data is beneficial for identification of novel genes, finding specialized functions associated with continuous biological events, and discovering transcriptionally distinct properties of defined stage-specific cell populations.

claims.claim: K-mean clustering gave new insights that divergent gene expression patterns contribute to different stages during in vitro myogenesis.

claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the clustering analysis.

claims.claim: RUNX1 has critical roles in hematopoiesis and leukemogenesis.

claims.evidence: This is established knowledge about RUNX1, with citation.

claims.claim: Cellular dysfunction in myotonic dystrophy 2 might be initiated even in the muscle stem/precursor cell stage, which could provide new insights to study MD2 pathogenesis.
claims.source: In an attempt to further analyze the stage-specific transcriptome regulation during human myogenesis, we applied weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) in five different cell types (Figure 6—figure supplement 2). WGCNA with stages-specific transcriptomes allowed us to define modules of genes that are continuously coregulated and to study their stage-specific variation during skeletal muscle differentiation. By including all expressed genes with expression variation, we identified a total of 92 modules defined as groups of genes coordinately expressed across 20 samples. These data imply that cellular dysfunction might be initiated even in the muscle stem/precursor cell stage, which could provide new insights to study MD2 pathogenesis.
claims.evidence: This is speculation about disease pathogenesis based on gene expression findings.

results.result: The study successfully generated and validated multiple genetic reporter hPSC lines (OCT4::EGFP, MSGN1::EGFP, PAX7::EGFP, MYOG::EGFP) and developed a novel myotube isolation method to purify five distinct cell populations representing sequential stages of human myogenesis in vitro. Each reporter line showed stage-specific EGFP expression with high percentages at appropriate timepoints, and purified populations exhibited enriched expression of corresponding marker genes validated by qRT-PCR and immunostaining.
results.evaluation: Claims C2, C19-C62 collectively demonstrate successful generation and validation of reporter lines with appropriate temporal expression patterns, enrichment of stage-specific markers in purified populations, and development of a functional myotube isolation method. The data include FACS analysis, qRT-PCR validation, immunostaining, and functional assays showing fusion ability, providing converging evidence for the reliability of the isolation strategy.

results.result: RNA-seq analysis of five purified cell populations revealed stage-specific transcriptional profiles with appropriate expression of marker genes, hierarchical clustering showing developmental relationships, and GO analysis identifying biological processes enriched at each stage. PAX7::EGFP+ and MYOG::EGFP+ cells showed both shared and distinct transcriptional features, with PAX7::EGFP+ cells enriched for signaling pathway genes and MYOG::EGFP+ cells enriched for muscle differentiation genes.
results.evaluation: Claims C63-C92 describe comprehensive RNA-seq analysis with appropriate quality metrics (83M total reads, 34M aligned reads), stage-specific marker expression, clustering analysis, PCA showing developmental trajectory, and GO analysis revealing biologically relevant processes. The data demonstrate transcriptional differences between PAX7::EGFP+ and MYOG::EGFP+ cells with enrichment of functionally relevant pathways.

results.result: K-means clustering of 22,939 genes into 10 clusters revealed distinct temporal expression patterns during myogenesis, with each cluster showing enrichment of functionally related genes and appropriate GO terms. Cluster 1 contained presomite markers (MSGN1, TBX6, T), Cluster 4 contained PAX7::EGFP+ cell markers (PAX7, MYF5, CD271, TWIST1), and Cluster 10 contained late myogenesis markers (MEF2C, MYOD1, TTN, DMD, RUNX1).
results.evaluation: Claims C93-C106 describe K-means clustering analysis validated by known marker genes showing appropriate temporal patterns, with GO analysis revealing biologically relevant processes for each cluster. The clustering successfully separated genes by developmental stage and identified both known and novel genes in each cluster.

results.result: CD271 was identified as a surface marker that overlaps with PAX7::EGFP+ cells (92.55±0.95% of PAX7::EGFP+ cells were CD271+), with CD271bright cells showing enriched expression of myogenic genes (PAX7, MYF5, MYOD1, MYOG) and sustained fusion ability during in vitro expansion comparable to PAX7::EGFP+ cells.
results.evaluation: Claims C107-C112 demonstrate that CD271 can serve as a marker for PAX7+ cells through FACS analysis showing high overlap, post-sort validation showing enriched myogenic gene expression, and functional assays showing sustained fusion ability over multiple passages. The data support CD271 as an alternative marker for isolating PAX7+ muscle progenitors.

results.result: RUNX1 was identified in Cluster 10 and shown to be expressed during late myogenic differentiation in myotubes and some myoblasts but not in PAX7+ cells. A RUNX1::EGFP reporter line showed 44.90±3.23% EGFP+ cells at days 30-35, with RUNX1::EGFP+ cells showing enriched expression of myotube markers (MEF2C, TTN, DMD) and minimal contamination from other lineages.
results.evaluation: Claims C113-C122 demonstrate RUNX1 expression during late myogenesis through clustering analysis, immunostaining showing expression in myotubes/myoblasts but not PAX7+ cells, generation and validation of a RUNX1::EGFP reporter line, and qRT-PCR showing enrichment of myotube markers and absence of other lineage markers in RUNX1::EGFP+ cells.

results.result: Three TWIST1 homozygous knockout clones were generated in the PAX7::EGFP reporter line, with complete loss of TWIST1 protein confirmed by western blot and immunostaining. TWIST1 KO did not affect formation of PAX7+ cells (9.29±0.68% vs 9.40±1.35% in WT), proliferation (69.88±3.49% Ki67+ cells), apoptosis, or myotube fusion ability.
results.evaluation: Claims C125-C132 demonstrate successful generation of TWIST1 KO lines with validated loss of protein expression, and show that TWIST1 deletion does not affect PAX7+ cell formation, proliferation, apoptosis, or terminal differentiation through FACS analysis, Ki67 staining, Annexin V analysis, and fusion index measurements.

results.result: TWIST1 knockout significantly reduced maintenance of PAX7::EGFP expression during in vitro expansion, with PAX7::EGFP+ cells declining from comparable levels at early passages to significantly lower levels at passage 4 (15.98±1.70% in KO vs 29.80±1.04% in WT, p<0.0001), demonstrating that TWIST1 is required for maintaining PAX7 expression in putative skeletal muscle progenitor cells.
results.evaluation: Claims C134-C136 show a specific and statistically significant effect of TWIST1 deletion on PAX7 expression maintenance during expansion, with appropriate controls showing no effect on proliferation or apoptosis. The progressive decline over passages with significant p-values at passages 2-4 supports a role for TWIST1 in maintaining PAX7 expression.

results.result: RNA-seq analysis of TWIST1 KO PAX7::EGFP+ cells revealed 643 differentially expressed genes compared to WT, with TWIST1 KO cells showing upregulation of genes related to Wnt signaling pathway (GO:0016055, p=7.63E-03), cell division, and RNA processing, while WT cells showed enrichment of skeletal muscle development genes.
results.evaluation: Claims C137-C145 describe comprehensive RNA-seq analysis showing transcriptional differences between WT and TWIST1 KO PAX7::EGFP+ cells, with PCA showing distinct clustering, identification of differentially expressed genes, and GO analysis revealing enrichment of Wnt signaling and other pathways in KO cells with appropriate p-values.

results.result: TWIST1 KO PAX7::EGFP+ cells showed upregulation of Wnt signaling target genes, and treatment of WT PAX7::EGFP+ cells with Wnt activator (CHIR99021) decreased PAX7::EGFP+ cells in a dose-dependent manner, mimicking the TWIST1 KO phenotype. However, Wnt inhibitor (XAV939) treatment of TWIST1 KO cells did not significantly rescue PAX7::EGFP expression.
results.evaluation: Claims C148-C151 show that Wnt activation mimics TWIST1 KO phenotype, suggesting involvement of Wnt signaling. However, the failure of Wnt inhibitor to rescue the phenotype (C150) indicates the relationship is more complex than simple pathway activation. The conclusion that TWIST1 is associated with Wnt signaling (C151) is supported, but the mechanistic relationship remains unclear.

results.result: DYSTROPHIN expression was detected at low levels in PAX7::EGFP+ cells by RNA-seq and confirmed by western blot, despite DYSTROPHIN being clustered in Cluster 10 (late myogenesis markers).
results.evaluation: Claims C177-C178 demonstrate DYSTROPHIN expression in PAX7::EGFP+ cells through both RNA-seq data and western blot validation using MANDYS1 antibody, providing converging evidence for expression at this earlier stage than expected from clustering analysis.

results.result: The study provides a comprehensive transcriptional landscape of hPSC-derived myogenesis and identifies TWIST1 as having a new role in maintaining PAX7 expression in human skeletal muscle progenitors, establishing a foundation for understanding transcriptional regulation of human myogenic ontogeny with potential applications for disease modeling and cell therapy.
results.evaluation: Claims C1, C5, C23, C152-C154, C202-C205 represent summary statements about the study's contributions. The major findings (transcriptional profiling of five stages, clustering analysis, identification of TWIST1 role) are well-supported by the experimental data. However, claims about future applications (C204, C205) are speculative.

results.result: PAX7::EGFP+ cells showed significantly low levels of neural crest markers SOX10 and PAX6 compared to hESC-derived neural crest cells, and no SOX10+ or AP2+ cells were detected by immunostaining in PAX7::EGFP+ cells.
results.evaluation: Claims C48-C49 demonstrate absence of neural crest contamination through qRT-PCR showing low expression of neural crest markers compared to positive control and immunostaining showing no detectable SOX10+ or AP2+ cells, providing appropriate negative controls for cell identity.

results.result: TWIST1 KO cells showed aberrant transcriptional patterns of PAX3, PAX7, MYF5, and MYOD1 during myogenic specification, despite comparable levels of PAX7::EGFP+ cells at days 25-30.
results.evaluation: Claim C133 describes aberrant gene expression patterns during differentiation in TWIST1 KO cells shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2A, indicating that TWIST1 affects transcriptional dynamics even when final PAX7+ cell percentages are similar. This suggests TWIST1 has roles beyond simply determining PAX7+ cell numbers.

results.result: The manuscript provides appropriate background on embryonic myogenesis stages, prior work on myogenic differentiation, key transcription factors (OCT4, MSGN1, MYOG, PAX7), and CRISPR/Cas9 technology for generating reporter lines, establishing the rationale for the study.
results.evaluation: Claims C6-C18, C24, C39, C155, C158 represent established knowledge and prior work appropriately cited to provide context. These background claims are well-supported by the cited literature and establish the foundation for the experimental approach.
